summary: Vanuatu waives visas for citizens of well over 100 countries — including the whole EU, the UK, US, Australia, New Zealand, China, India and its Pacific neighbors — for stays of up to 120 days, while everyone else applies for a visitor e-Visa allowing about 30 days.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your intended departure from Vanuatu.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 1 year and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services

vaccinations.name: Malaria prevention
vaccinations.text: Malaria risk is low but present on the northern islands such as Espiritu Santo, Malekula and Ambae; Port Vila and Tanna are considered malaria-free. Ask a travel clinic about prophylaxis if you are heading north, and use repellent everywhere against dengue.

source.name: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not a condition of entry, but hospital care is basic and serious cases are flown to Australia or New Zealand. Coverage for medical evacuation, diving and cyclone disruption is strongly recommended.

source.name: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services

onwardTicket.text: Visitors must hold a confirmed onward or return ticket; airlines check it at boarding and immigration officers may ask to see it.

source.name: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services

proofOfFunds.text: You must be able to show sufficient funds and confirmed accommodation for your stay. No fixed sum is published — a booking confirmation plus a card or bank statement normally satisfies the officer.

source.name: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services

declarations.name: Passenger arrival and customs declaration card
declarations.text: Complete the immigration and customs arrival card issued before landing at Port Vila or Luganville, declaring food, plant and animal products and any cash above the reporting threshold.

source.name: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services

currencyLimits.text: Cash above the declaration threshold set by Vanuatu Customs must be reported on arrival and departure. The country's financial-center status means these rules are enforced, so check the current amount before traveling with large sums.

source.name: Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services

notes: Biosecurity is strict: fresh produce, seeds, plants, meat, and used camping, hiking or dive gear must be declared and may be treated.
Firearms and ammunition require prior police approval; drug offenses carry heavy penalties.
Exporting coral, giant clam shell, turtle products or cultural artefacts without a permit is prohibited.

payments.text: Cards work in Port Vila and Luganville hotels, restaurants, dive shops and supermarkets, and ATMs are available in both towns. Outside them — Tanna, Pentecost, the outer islands — it is cash only, so carry vatu in small notes.

safety.text: Vanuatu is welcoming with low levels of violent crime; petty theft in Port Vila and occasional unrest are the main concerns. Natural hazards are the bigger factor: cyclones from November to April, frequent earthquakes, and active volcanoes on Tanna and Ambrym.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Vanuatu travel information

bestTimeToVisit.text: April to October is the cooler, drier season, outside the cyclone months and best for diving, hiking Mount Yasur and the Espiritu Santo blue holes.

tips.text: The EU's suspension of its visa-waiver agreement with Vanuatu, over the citizenship-by-investment scheme, affects Vanuatu passport holders traveling to Europe. It does not affect EU citizens visiting Vanuatu, who still enter without a visa.

Cyclone season runs November to April and Vanuatu is one of the most disaster-exposed countries in the world. Travel in those months with flexible bookings and insurance that covers cancellation and evacuation.

Mount Yasur on Tanna and Ambrym's craters are active and their alert levels change at short notice. Go with a licensed guide and check the current level with the Vanuatu Meteorology and Geo-hazards Department before booking.
Unusually for the Pacific, Vanuatu drives on the right — a legacy of the Anglo-French condominium. Take extra care if you have arrived from Australia, New Zealand or Fiji.

Land, beaches and sites such as waterfalls, blue holes and land-diving towers are customary property. Expect a modest fee in vatu paid to the landowner, and always ask before photographing people or ceremonies.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Vanuatu?
faq.answer: Most travelers do not. Citizens of all EU states, the UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, China, Japan, India, South Africa, the Gulf states and Vanuatu's Pacific neighbors are visa-exempt for stays of up to 120 days. Nationalities not on the exemption list apply for a visitor e-Visa before traveling, which allows around 30 days.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Vanuatu without a visa?
faq.answer: Up to 120 days for visa-exempt nationalities. In practice the immigration officer decides the period granted and often stamps a shorter initial stay, so check what is in your passport and apply to the Department of Immigration in Port Vila if you need longer.

faq.question: Has the EU suspended visa-free travel with Vanuatu?
faq.answer: Yes, but only in one direction. The EU suspended its short-stay visa-waiver agreement over Vanuatu's citizenship-by-investment program, which means Vanuatu passport holders now need a Schengen visa for Europe. EU citizens traveling to Vanuatu are unaffected and still enter without a visa.

faq.question: How does the Vanuatu e-Visa work?
faq.answer: Travelers from countries outside the exemption list apply online to the Department of Immigration before departure, uploading a passport copy, itinerary, accommodation booking and onward ticket. Allow at least two to three weeks, and apply only through official government channels.

faq.question: What will I be asked for on arrival?
faq.answer: A passport valid 6 months beyond your departure, a confirmed onward or return ticket, proof of accommodation and funds, and a completed arrival and customs card. Biosecurity checks on food, seeds and used outdoor equipment are taken seriously.
